implementation_plan.description: Verify current branch is feature/single-player-minimax-ai (git branch --show-current). Confirm game.js already has minimax, getBestMove, difficulty, gameMode, scheduleAIMove, setGameMode. Confirm index.html has mode-switcher HTML and CSS. No baseline changes needed.

Fix difficulty percentage discrepancy in game.js getBestMove(): change Easy from 80% random to 100% random by removing the easy-specific minimax fallthrough (just always return randomMove() for 'easy'); change Medium threshold from Math.random()<0.40 to Math.random()<0.60 so Medium is 60% random / 40% minimax, matching the feature specification.

Change the default `difficulty` module-level variable in game.js from 'hard' to 'medium'. This aligns with the UX convention that Medium is the default selected difficulty when the difficulty selector first appears.

Add `setDifficulty(diff)` function to game.js in the 'New Game / Reset Score / Mode' section. It: (1) sets `difficulty = diff`, (2) queries all .diff-btn elements and removes .active class from each, (3) adds .active class to the button whose data-difficulty attribute matches diff. Does NOT restart the game — takes effect on next AI move.

Modify setGameMode() in game.js to also show/hide the difficulty selector element. After updating the mode button states, add: `const diffSel = document.getElementById('difficultySelector'); if (diffSel) diffSel.classList.toggle('hidden', mode !== 'single');`. This ensures difficulty selector is only visible in single-player mode.

Modify init() in game.js to cache and bind difficulty button events. After the existing btn1p/btn2p bindings, add: `document.querySelectorAll('.diff-btn').forEach(btn => { btn.addEventListener('click', () => setDifficulty(btn.dataset.difficulty)); });`. Also call setDifficulty('medium') at the end of init() to ensure the medium button starts with .active class when the difficulty selector first renders.
Update module.exports in game.js to add setDifficulty to the exported symbols. Also update _getState to include the current difficulty value so test harnesses can inspect it.

Add CSS for the difficulty selector in index.html's <style> block, placed immediately after the existing mode-switcher CSS rules (before responsive tweaks). New rules: (a) `.difficulty-selector` — same pill container style as .mode-switcher (flex row, bg-surface, color-border, border-radius 999px, padding 4px, width fit-content); (b) `.diff-btn` — same base style as .mode-btn (transparent background, color-muted, rounded, transitions on color/box-shadow 0.15s ease); (c) `.diff-btn:focus-visible` — same neon focus ring as .mode-btn:focus-visible; (d) `.diff-btn.active[data-difficulty='easy']` — color:#00ff88, box-shadow:0 0 8px #00ff8866, inner border via outline:1px solid #00ff88; (e) `.diff-btn.active[data-difficulty='medium']` — color:var(--color-o), outline:1px solid var(--color-o), box-shadow:0 0 8px var(--color-o-glow); (f) `.diff-btn.active[data-difficulty='hard']` — color:var(--color-x), outline:1px solid var(--color-x), box-shadow:0 0 8px var(--color-x-glow); (g) `.difficulty-selector.hidden { display: none; }`. (h) Add .diff-btn to the prefers-reduced-motion transition-duration:0.01ms block.

Add HTML for the difficulty selector to index.html, inserted immediately after the closing tag of the mode-switcher div and before the opening of #board. Structure: `<div class='difficulty-selector hidden' id='difficultySelector' role='group' aria-label='AI difficulty'>` containing three buttons: `<button class='diff-btn' data-difficulty='easy' type='button' aria-pressed='false'>Easy</button>`, `<button class='diff-btn active' data-difficulty='medium' type='button' aria-pressed='true'>Medium</button>`, `<button class='diff-btn' data-difficulty='hard' type='button' aria-pressed='false'>Hard</button>`. The selector starts hidden because game mode defaults to 2-player. Medium starts with .active class and aria-pressed='true' to match the default difficulty.

Update GAME_HTML fixture in __tests__/game.dom.test.js to include the new difficulty-selector HTML element (matching the structure added to index.html). Without this, init() will run querySelectorAll('.diff-btn') on a document that lacks those elements, and setDifficulty() will silently no-op instead of setting active states. All existing test assertions remain unchanged.

Write __tests__/ai.difficulty.test.js: pure-logic unit tests for getBestMove() difficulty tiers and the corrected Easy/Medium percentages. Uses Jest node environment (no DOM). Test cases per test_plan section.

Write __tests__/ai.difficulty-ui.test.js: DOM integration tests for difficulty selector UI using Jest + jsdom. Includes its own GAME_HTML fixture (mode-switcher + difficulty-selector + board). Test cases per test_plan section.
Run full test suite: `npm test` to confirm all existing tests plus new tests pass. Run `npx playwright test` to verify E2E tests. Fix any regressions before committing.

new_files.purpose: Pure unit tests for getBestMove() difficulty dispatch logic using Jest node environment (no DOM required). Validates: Easy always returns a random cell (never the optimal minimax move), Medium exhibits ~40% optimal move rate (statistical test with tolerance), Hard always picks the optimal move (blocking win, taking win). Also verifies getBestMove() never mutates the passed boardState and returns -1 on full boards.

DOM integration tests for the difficulty selector UI using Jest + jsdom. Validates: initial state (difficulty selector hidden, Medium button has .active), switching to 1player mode reveals difficulty selector, switching back to 2player hides it, clicking Easy sets Easy .active and removes Medium .active, clicking Hard sets Hard .active, setDifficulty() updates the difficulty module state accessed via _getState(), AI moves in 1player mode respect the selected difficulty (Hard always blocks X's win).

rollback_plan:
All changes are confined to feature/single-player-minimax-ai branch, isolated from main. Rollback options:

1. DISCARD UNCOMMITTED CHANGES: git restore index.html game.js __tests__/game.dom.test.js; git clean -fd __tests__/ai.difficulty.test.js __tests__/ai.difficulty-ui.test.js

2. PER-COMMIT REVERT: git revert <commit-hash> creates an undo commit preserving history (safe for shared branches).

3. BRANCH RESET: git reset --hard <last-good-sha> — use git log --oneline to identify SHA. The last clean SHA before this feature's commits is available in git log.

4. FULL BRANCH DELETION: git branch -D feature/single-player-minimax-ai and recreate from main if abandoned.

5. POST-MERGE (worst case): git revert -m 1 <merge-commit-sha> on main.

Risk profile: NARROW — modifies getBestMove() percentages (existing logic, low risk), adds setDifficulty() (new function, no side-effects on existing code paths), modifies setGameMode() to show/hide one new element (guarded by null check). Two new CSS blocks and one new HTML element added. Two new test files. Zero dependency changes.

risk_assessment.risk: Changing Easy from 80% to 100% random or Medium from 60% to 40% minimax breaks existing AI unit tests that assumed the old percentages
risk_assessment.likelihood: Medium if existing tests hardcode the old thresholds
risk_assessment.mitigation: Review __tests__/game.ai.test.js and __tests__/game.singleplayer.test.js for percentage-specific assertions; update statistical bounds to match new spec. Run npm test after each change.

risk_assessment.risk: setGameMode() calling getElementById('difficultySelector') returning null if element isn't in the DOM during tests
risk_assessment.mitigation: setGameMode() wraps difficultySelector access in `if (diffSel)` guard. GAME_HTML in test files updated to include the element.

risk_assessment.risk: Difficulty selector showing in 2-player mode if setGameMode() is called before difficulty-selector HTML is added
risk_assessment.likelihood: None — game defaults to 2-player with hidden selector
risk_assessment.mitigation: Difficulty selector HTML includes 'hidden' class by default. setGameMode() only removes 'hidden' when mode === 'single'.

risk_assessment.risk: CSS sibling combinator (.turn-indicator.is-x ~ .board) affected by inserting difficulty-selector element between turn-indicator and board
risk_assessment.mitigation: General sibling combinator (~) matches ANY subsequent sibling. Inserting elements between turn-indicator and board does not affect the hover glow rule.

risk_assessment.risk: setDifficulty() called before DOM is ready (during module load) causing null querySelectorAll errors
risk_assessment.likelihood: None — setDifficulty() only called from init() (after DOMContentLoaded) and click handlers
risk_assessment.mitigation: Function is never called at module-load time. The module-level `difficulty = 'medium'` variable is set statically; setDifficulty() just syncs the UI to match.

risk_assessment.risk: Default difficulty changing from 'hard' to 'medium' causing Hard-mode-dependent tests to use wrong difficulty
risk_assessment.mitigation: Tests that require a specific difficulty should call _setState({ difficulty: 'hard' }) or setDifficulty('hard') explicitly rather than relying on the default. Review existing single-player tests.
